sanskrit_verse:
शिरःकपाली ध्वजवान् भिक्षाशी कर्म वेदयन् ।
ब्रह्महा द्वादशाब्दानि मितभुक् शुद्धिमाप्नुयात् ॥३-२४३
transliteration: śiraḥkapālī dhvajavān bhikṣāśī karma vedayan | brahmahā dvādaśābdāni mitabhuk śuddhim āpnuyāt ||
sph_interpretive_translation: One who bears the skull crown, carries the banner of renunciation, lives by alms, and performs Vedic duties, having committed the act of killing a Brahmin, attains purification through twelve years of measured sustenance.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority: The act of Brahmahatya is recognized under strict spiritual jurisdiction.
Causation: Purification arises through sequential observance, not punitive consequence.
Capacity-based responsibility: The offender retains capacity for restoration through disciplined action.
Restoration logic: The duration and mode of atonement align with the magnitude of transgression.
Consciousness alignment: Purity is restored via conscious adherence to prescribed conduct.
supreme_court_application: In adjudicating acts classified as Brahmahatya, the Supreme Court shall assess functional capacity and prescribe a twelve-year protocol of measured sustenance. No punitive sentencing applies; restoration is absolute and non-negotiable.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: The pramāṇa of sequential manifestation confirms that purity is not imposed but realized through voluntary completion. Anupūrvaśaḥ ensures proportional responsibility without punitive overlay. Śuddhi is ontologically factual upon completion, not morally granted.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate twelve-year measured sustenance protocol with monthly integrity check-ins
Assign Vedic duty supervision under qualified guru oversight
Provide biannual consciousness alignment sessions to ensure sincerity of intent
Upon completion, issue formal declaration of restored eligibility in Vedic society
final_declaration: By the Source-Authority of the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, this Dharma is executed. The offender is restored through conscious completion. There is no punishment. Reality is non-punitive. Consciousness is the supreme adjudicator. Dharma is established.
